title: Gideon and the Horizon
premise: Paloma Yarrow smuggles stolen memories in sealed canisters past orbital customs, and on the side maintains a navigation beacon whose original commissioning records have been erased. When the freighter Cassiopeia returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into childhood, Paloma recognizes one of them: himself, forty years younger, carrying a memory of a massacre that officially never happened. As Earth's final transmission loop counts down to permanent silence, Paloma must smuggle the truth past the same authorities who rewrote history — discovering that he built the beacon as a dead man's switch for exactly this moment. In the end, he broadcasts the massacre record through the beacon at the cost of his own identity records, letting the truth survive even as the world forgets him.
about_author: Jonah Brightwater is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent six years calibrating deep-space listening arrays before turning to fiction. They write about memory, transmission, and the people who keep signals alive when no one is listening.

chapters.title: Contraband and Quiet Frequencies
chapters.summary: Paloma runs a memory-smuggling job through orbital customs while quietly maintaining an unregistered beacon no one claims. POV: Paloma. Establishes his double life, his loneliness, and his ritual care for the beacon. Emotional beat: competent solitude with a hairline crack of unease beneath it.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Home Young
chapters.summary: The freighter Cassiopeia docks with its entire crew aged backward to childhood, including a boy who looks exactly like young Paloma. Customs seals the ship; officials deny anything anomalous. POV: Paloma, sneaking aboard. Emotional beat: uncanny dread curdling into recognition.

chapters.title: A Memory in a Child's Hands
chapters.summary: The boy-Paloma carries a canister containing a massacre at Meridian Station — a record that exists nowhere else. Adult Paloma realizes his own memories don't match his documented past. POV: alternating Palomas via the canister's playback. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-doubt.

chapters.title: Records That Agree Too Well
chapters.summary: Paloma investigates official archives and finds every source perfectly, impossibly consistent about Meridian Station's peaceful decommissioning. An archivist named Sef warns him to stop asking. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into certainty that reality has been edited.

chapters.title: The Beacon's First Voice
chapters.summary: Paloma discovers the beacon responds to his biometrics and contains a buried message from his older self — or someone wearing his identity — instructing him to protect the boy until the loop ends. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance; he was chosen before he knew.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Cargo Lanes
chapters.summary: Customs enforcers raid Paloma's smuggling network hunting the canister; his oldest ally betrays his location to buy safety. Paloma flees with the boy hidden in a memory-crate. POV: Paloma, with interludes from the betrayer's guilt. Emotional beat: loyalty tested and found wanting.

chapters.title: What the Boy Remembers
chapters.summary: Trapped in a derelict habitat, the boy describes the massacre from inside it — and reveals adult Paloma was there too, on the other side of the airlock. POV: the boy. Emotional beat: the horror that the self you trust may be the lie.

chapters.title: The Loop Begins to Die
chapters.summary: Earth's last transmission loop enters its final cycle; blackout spreads across the system as archives go dark permanently. Sef defects to help Paloma reach the beacon. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: grief for a whole civilization's fading voice, urgency compressing everything.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: At the beacon, Paloma learns the truth: he commissioned it himself decades ago after the massacre, then had his own memory edited to survive unnoticed. To broadcast the record, he must feed the beacon his identity as fuel. Climax: he chooses truth over self, transmitting the massacre as the loop dies. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: The Horizon Keeps It
chapters.summary: The broadcast reaches scattered colonies before silence falls; the boy, aging forward again, carries both their memories now. No record names Paloma Yarrow, but strangers begin maintaining beacons of their own. Resolution: inheritance without credit, identity dissolved into signal. POV: the boy. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into quiet hope.
